clue.text: Article in Times left unfinished without a herb used in soups

indicators.note: in tells us the article sits inside the word for times

parts.note: as in four by two, by means times when multiplying
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cut word wraps round a
the word left loses its final letter, being not finished

explanation.surface: A newspaper article left half-written, complaining that a soup recipe lacks its herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is multiplication (four by two), not the newspaper. 'unfinished' trims the word left by its last letter, and 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic leaf of the laurel is a standard flavouring dropped into soups and stews.

clue.text: A very old poster in firm's green

indicators.note: in places the advert inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
an AD, advertisement, can be a poster

explanation.surface: An ancient poster belonging to a company with environmental, green credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocado is the name of a dull yellowish-green colour, after the fruit's skin and flesh.

clue.text: Most of French paper's yellow

indicators.note: most of signals the paper's name is cut short at its end

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading French daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Comment on the colour of a French newspaper's pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final DE from LE MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is a pale bright shade of yellow, named after the citrus fruit's skin.

clue.text: Coach unable to accommodate male, 16

indicators.note: accommodate means take in, so the reworked letters house the male letter
to coach is to train or knock into shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A coach who can't fit one more man on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' is the anagram signal, not a vehicle or trainer: UNABLE is rearranged as ALBUEN, and 'to accommodate' takes M inside it. The definition is 16 across, WHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg, the clear part that turns white when cooked.

clue.text: One feeds three queens

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
three queens means the cat plus two more, each ER, Elizabeth Regina, the crossword's standard queen

explanation.surface: A curious statement that someone is feeding three queens, perhaps at a royal banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat, and ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's standard queen, used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer is a person or firm who supplies food for events, so one who feeds others.

clue.text: Cite a fruit extract that's talked about by some

indicators.note: said aloud in some accents, so the phrase is heard, not read; only some speakers make the match

parts.note: juice is extracted from fruit; with a, the phrase a juice

explanation.surface: Quote a fruit juice that people chatter about.
explanation.walkthrough: In accents that sound 'adduce' as a-JOOS, the answer sounds like 'a juice'; 'by some' admits that not every speaker hears it so.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to bring forward evidence or examples, much as one cites them in argument.

clue.text: Colonist guzzling new prince's dairy product

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing, so the colonist takes the letter inside

parts.note: an emmet is an old dialect word for an ant, which lives in a colony
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: A settler greedily eating a young prince's cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonist' is not a human settler but an ant, EMMET, a member of a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes, made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Austere English composer's blocking film

indicators.note: blocking means standing in the way, so the composer's name fills the gap inside the film

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia; with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: A stern English composer prevents a film from going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's is not a link here: it supplies a letter that the composer's name carries into the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and sincere, close in sense to grave or austere in manner.

clue.text: Battered dish? He loathed it on toast

indicators.note: something that is toast is ruined or done for, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone who hated a dish served on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' belongs to the letters, and 'toast' is slang for finished, the anagram signal. TOAD IN THE HOLE is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is literally cooked in batter, hence battered; the question mark flags the pun on beaten.

clue.text: It emerges from opening a 12, initially

definitions.text: It emerges from opening a 12, initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each word, with 12 standing for its answer

parts.note: 12 across is MAGNUM, the big bottle

explanation.surface: Description of what bubbles out when a magnum of champagne is uncorked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 must be read as its answer, MAGNUM, whose first letter is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth and bubbles rush out when a large bottle of champagne is uncorked.

clue.text: Drink left over in group refreshed army

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the group word

parts.note: a body is a group, as in a body of people
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

indicators.note: refreshed means made new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink left over within a group of soldiers just refreshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refreshed' rearranges ARMY into MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice, a classic named drink.

clue.text: Parent drinks a gin, disposing of one big bottle

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the parent swallows the remaining letters

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so a letter goes from a gin

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother drinking gin and getting rid of the empty big bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' removes I from AGIN to leave AGN, which 'drinks' puts inside MUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle twice the standard size, holding one and a half litres.

clue.text: Tin in hamper, second container of 25?

indicators.note: in places the tin inside the word for hamper

parts.note: to hamper is to hinder or deter
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A tin packed in a picnic hamper, the second vessel for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' is a verb, not a basket. 25 is RIOJA, poured from its bottle into a second container.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is poured from its bottle into a decanter, so that is its second container.

clue.text: Leader to lead with three articles

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
an, an and a are three indefinite articles, joined in that order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a leader: lead with three articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, symbol Pb, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang for the most important person, the boss in charge.

clue.text: Result of eating too much beef?

definitions.meaning: to beef is to complain; beef also tempts toward the meat eaten

explanation.surface: Musing on what overdoing the roast beef leads to.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellyache is a stomach pain; as a verb it means to grumble, as does beef.

clue.text: Pale Guardian covers bestseller with renewed energy

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so the paper's pronoun goes round the bestseller

parts.note: this newspaper, the Guardian, refers to itself as we in its editorials
a hit is a bestseller

explanation.surface: The Guardian runs a bestseller with fresh energy, though it looks pale.
explanation.walkthrough: A second wordplay follows: 'with renewed' rearranges WITH, plus E for 'energy', also giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: White describes something pale or lacking colour, as a frightened face goes white.

clue.text: Carpet that is ancient, small and austere

parts.note: austere and cold both mean unwelcoming and severe

explanation.surface: Describing a rug that is antique, small and plain.
explanation.walkthrough: A second wordplay comes first: SC (scilicet, 'that is') plus OLD for 'ancient' also gives the answer. 'Carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in for a reprimand, to tell them off.

clue.text: Transport about half of veal where it's sliced?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the transport word goes round the half

parts.note: to carry is to transport

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: Carrying veal off to where the meat is carved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the meat: a carvery is a restaurant where roast joints are carved to order.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a restaurant counter where roast meat is sliced in front of diners.

clue.text: Fruit in soft drink that's oddly part of 9, maybe?

indicators.note: in places the fruit inside the drink

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
a hip is the fruit of the rose

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of that

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit floating in a fizzy drink, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is TOAD IN THE HOLE, sausages in batter; a chipolata is a small sausage that may be used.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a thin sausage, one possible ingredient in toad in the hole, hence maybe.

clue.text: Staff regularly asleep? It's the drink

parts.note: a pale is a stake or post, a staff

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of asleep

explanation.surface: A staff member regularly nodding off: drink is the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is not employees but a stick, PALE, as in a fence paling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale ale is a light-coloured beer, a familiar pub drink.

clue.text: Cross to put outside old Islington pub

indicators.note: put outside means the word to wraps round the pub

parts.note: the Angel was a famous coaching inn in Islington, London, which gave its name to the area

explanation.surface: A grumpy instruction to throw someone out of an old London pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is not angry but a hybrid: a tangelo is a cross between tangerine and pomelo.
explanation.definitionFit: The tangelo is a citrus hybrid, bred by crossing a tangerine with a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Seethe a short way into series

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the pieces go inside the abbreviation for series

parts.note: a means one, the Roman numeral I
mm, millimetre, is a short distance

explanation.surface: Seething about being only partway through a TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' stands for one, I, not the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To simmer is to be quietly angry, just short of boiling over, like seething.

clue.text: 29's wi-fi picked up bang outside

indicators.note: outside means the bang word goes round the sound-alike

parts.note: a crash is a loud bang

indicators.note: picked up as a signal is received, so the word wi-fi is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: wi-fi is said aloud as why-fie, written Y FI

explanation.surface: A lobster's wi-fi signal gets interrupted by a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is DECAPOD; the 's is 'is'. 'picked up' makes WI-FI sound as Y and FI, placed inside CRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayfish is a ten-legged crustacean, so it is an example of a decapod.

clue.text: Cat grabs a radio's top sound producer

indicators.note: grabs means seizes and holds, so the cat holds the letters inside

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: top in a down light, here meaning the head or first letter of radio

explanation.surface: A cat snatches the top off a radio, which makes sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx, the voice box, houses the vocal cords that produce speech.

clue.text: A carpenter from the south put away nearly new wine

indicators.note: in a down light reading from the south means reading upward, so backwards
put away means removed, so letters are taken from joiner

parts.note: a joiner is a carpenter

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter goes from new

explanation.surface: A carpenter from the south puts away a nearly new wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts NEW to NE, 'put away' removes that from JOINER to leave JOIR, and 'from the south' reverses A JOIR upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: PM devouring every island's dessert

indicators.note: devouring means eating up, so the two letters hold the next word inside

parts.note: PM is the abbreviation for prime minister
each and every are synonyms
Elba is the island of Napoleon's first exile

explanation.surface: The prime minister eats every island dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba is a dessert of peaches, raspberry sauce and ice cream named after Nellie Melba.

clue.text: Almost completed northern range

indicators.note: almost signals the word loses its final letter

parts.note: over means finished or completed

explanation.surface: A northern mountain range nearly fully explored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' is not mountains but a kitchen stove, whose oven is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large cooking stove, so an oven is a reasonable stand-in.

clue.text: From memory, boy's gutted, given red card

indicators.note: gutted means emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters of boy

parts.note: hearts are a red suit, so a heart is a red card

explanation.surface: A footballer devastated at being sent off with a red card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red card' is not the football sending-off but a playing card in the red suit of hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing something by heart means having it memorised and able to recite it.

clue.text: Cook stepped around lobster for one

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
paced means stepped or walked

explanation.surface: A chef walking round a lobster in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses DOPACED to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobster has ten legs, making it one example of a decapod crustacean.
